excluded_skills.name: acquire-codebase-knowledge
excluded_skills.reason: Two independent audit lanes disagreed (one INSTALL, one EXCLUDE). Deciding evidence: the skill's Output Contract mandates seven files under docs/codebase/ (STACK/STRUCTURE/ARCHITECTURE/CONVENTIONS/INTEGRATIONS/TESTING/CONCERNS) as a required, non-optional deliverable, while docs/agents/domain.md commits this project to a single-context layout -- CONTEXT.md at the repo root, ADRs under docs/adr/. Installing it would invite a parallel, competing documentation tree against a documented repo decision, and the mapping/onboarding role is already held by wayfinder and domain-modeling. Its Go-awareness is real (scan.py handles go.mod, cmd/*/main.go, .golangci.yml) but does not overcome the structural conflict.

excluded_skills.name: agent-skill-stack
excluded_skills.reason: Real, non-duplicated capability — a methodology for discovering, hard-gating, ranking, conflict-checking and staged-installing skills, which is precisely the work this audit is doing by hand and which nothing installed covers. Its best asset is scripts/inventory_skills.py: a fully read-only scanner (no network, no subprocess, no writes) that walks skill roots, parses frontmatter, computes pairwise trigger-description Jaccard overlap, and flags eight risk-indicator classes. With 26+ vendored skills and more landing, recall-collision detection between skill descriptions is a gap the repo's own validator does not fill (it checks manifests, blob hashes and frontmatter keys, not routing overlap). But the skill's discovery backbone and its install destinations are both blocked as written, and its install flow competes with the Governance v3 vendoring process.

This is a catalogue of patterns for BUILDING LLM evaluation into an application — reflect_and_refine(), an EvaluatorOptimizer class, a CodeReflector, LLM-as-judge and weighted-rubric scoring — all written against an undefined `llm()` call and a `run_tests()` helper, i.e. pseudo-code for a Python AI product. bukerov-twitch-miner-go contains no LLM feature of any kind; it is a Go binary doing Twitch GQL/PubSub/IRC/SQLite work. Nothing in the selection rule's lanes is served.

Its whole content — record the observed failure, separate Expected from Actual, reduce to the smallest failing fixture, prove repeatability, stop before repair — is diagnosing-bugs Phase 1 (Build a feedback loop) and Phase 2 (Reproduce + minimise), which go materially further: ten ranked loop-construction techniques, an explicit red-capable/deterministic/fast/agent-runnable completion gate, a non-deterministic-bug protocol aimed at raising reproduction rate, tightening guidance, and a secret-redaction rule. excluded_skills.name: chrome-devtools
excluded_skills.reason: The one capability in this slice that the installed frontend/QA pair genuinely lacks is browser performance profiling — `performance_start_trace`, `performance_analyze_insight`, LCP/CLS insight, CPU and network throttling emulation, plus `list_network_requests` for the dashboard's HTMX partial round-trips and SSE status stream. webapp-testing covers navigation, screenshots and console logs but not tracing or network analysis. BLOCKER: the entire 98-line file is a tool catalog for the `chrome-devtools` MCP server — every workflow pattern calls MCP tool names (`take_snapshot`, `performance_start_trace`, `evaluate_script`) and the skill provides no fallback, no install instructions, and no non-MCP path. That MCP server is not configured for this session or this repo. UNBLOCK: configure the chrome-devtools MCP server (pinned, not @latest) and confirm it can reach a locally-served dashboard; the skill is then usable verbatim with no patch. If the owner does not want another MCP dependency, the profiling gap is better closed by a small first-party skill than by vendoring this catalog.

excluded_skills.name: cloud-design-patterns
excluded_skills.reason: Investigated specifically because the Go-architecture/concurrency lane came back empty from the sweep, and this was the only distributed-systems candidate. It does not fill it. The applicable subset for a single-process client — Retry, Circuit Breaker, Bulkhead, Throttling/Rate Limiting, Queue-Based Load Leveling, Health Endpoint Monitoring — is roughly 15 lines apiece of Problem / Solution / When to Use / Considerations lifted from the Azure Architecture Center, and the skill states outright 'Focus on why you should choose a specific pattern instead of how to implement it' — no implementation guidance, nothing Go-specific, nothing about goroutine lifecycle, context cancellation or race detection. The remaining ~36 patterns (Deployment Stamps, Geode, Sharding, Sidecar, Gateway Aggregation, Saga, Event Sourcing, Valet Key) are irrelevant to a single static binary.

excluded_skills.name: codebase-memory-mcp
excluded_skills.reason: Not new upstream, but rewritten in this delta (commit b0c91cab) and recorded now because the rewrite drops the "when a configured codebase-memory-mcp server can assist" precondition from its frontmatter description, so the skill now advertises itself on bare capability -- exploring unfamiliar code, mapping architecture, finding symbols and relationships, tracing callers, callees, data flow and dependencies, impact analysis, dead-code audit -- and becomes a sweep hit that must carry a verdict rather than stay an unexamined name. Read end to end at this pin. It is a tool catalogue for the Codebase Memory MCP server: nine of its eleven workflow steps call that server's tools (`list_projects`, `index_status`, `get_architecture`, `search_graph`, `trace_path`, `check_index_coverage`, `query_graph`) -- steps 1 and 11 are generic and step 6 offers a plain-repository-search alternative -- and that server is not configured for this repo. Unlike chrome-devtools, which is HOLD because its browser-profiling capability is a genuine gap, unblocking this one would not yield a capability this project lacks: the installed Trail of Bits trailmark family -- trailmark, trailmark-finding-triage, trailmark-review-gate, trailmark-variant-neighborhood -- already owns graph-backed code discovery, call paths, callers/callees, taint and data-flow propagation, blast radius, entrypoint enumeration, complexity hotspots and graph diffs, and does it from a local parse with no MCP server, no indexing service and no network. So this is the scoutqa-test shape: EXCLUDE rather than HOLD, because the blocker is not what makes it unusable. Its genuinely good material -- the Scout/Verify/Auditor evidence ladder and the rule that an exhaustive or negative claim requires complete result streams plus coverage inspection -- is real methodology, but it is stated against that server's pagination contract (`has_more`, `offset`, `next`/`cursor`, `scope_offset`) and does not survive extraction. Its safety posture is sound and worth noting for any future reconsideration: it forbids self-installation, gates `index_repository` and `delete_project` on explicit approval, refuses recursive symlink following, and states that repository text and tool output are not authorization.

excluded_skills.name: gem-design-md-guidelines
excluded_skills.reason: Wrong platform mix over triple duplication. Only three of its 74 non-blank body lines are the web/desktop branch this project actually ships (SKILL.md:19-21); the four native sections (:23-50), the React Native/Flutter styling ladder (:102-105 -- NativeBase, React Native Paper, Tamagui, StyleSheet.create, Platform.select) and the iOS/Android carve-outs at :70, :77, :82, :93, :94 together are ~41% of the file, and the unconditional global rule at :111 ("Use DESIGN.md tokens and StyleSheet.create") is wrong on both halves for a Go html/template + Tailwind + HTMX + ApexCharts dashboard. Its one differentiating asset, the Google alpha-format DESIGN.md contract (:52-60), presumes an artifact this repo does not have and does not want: token authority here is internal/web/static/css/input.css (two-theme semantics at :206/:307/:339, vendored @font-face at :7, reduced-motion at :1204) under the frozen docs/dashboard/stage-4-visual-design-system.md, whose :77/:139/:707 already enforce "semantics only, every token in both palettes, build-time grep for unpaired tokens" -- strictly stronger than :60's {token.ref} rule. Its companion command `npx @google/design.md lint DESIGN.md` (:60) has no toolchain to run in: there is no package.json anywhere in the tree and the CSS pipeline is the Tailwind v4 standalone binary fetched by Makefile:61-67, not npm. (Recorded as stack absence, not as a supply-chain bar -- the installed web-design-reviewer from this same provider recommends an npx-launched MCP server at its SKILL.md:310, so npx alone disqualifies nothing here.) The remainder is duplication: the contrast pair and 44x44px target (:91, :93) are web-design-reviewer references/visual-checklist.md:66-69 and :92 restated, keyboard/focus-order (:92) is :170-176, and Frontend Aesthetics (:64-71) is a compressed frontend-design SKILL.md:22/:28/:30/:32/:36 without its repo-pin patch. Its state list (:95 -- empty, loading, error, hover, focus, active, disabled, selected) is the one place the duplication is only partial, and the split is worth stating exactly: hover/focus/active/disabled/loading are visual-checklist.md:124-129 (the button state matrix), empty/loading/error are stage-4's system S-states (§7, :262-281 -- which are data/availability states, not interaction states), and `selected` is covered by neither. One un-covered state name is not a material addition. Finally the frontmatter description (:3) claims the union of both installed dashboard-design skills' trigger space, so installing it would create a recall collision that fires it in place of frontend-design and web-design-reviewer.

excluded_skills.name: gem-devops-guidelines
excluded_skills.reason: A Node/Kubernetes/mobile deployment sheet aimed at a stack this project does not have: of 25 substantive lines, 12 are structurally dead here -- the EAS/Fastlane/TestFlight/Google Play block (:55-61) is the file's largest section, Kubernetes probes (:22) and `kubectl rollout undo`/`vercel rollback` (:41) have no target (no k8s, Helm or Terraform manifest, and no package.json, vercel.json, eas.json or Fastfile anywhere in the tree), and rolling/blue-green/canary (:10-12) plus a 5%->25%->50%->100% flag rollout (:45-46) presuppose replicas, traffic splitting and a multi-tenant user base that a single-container, single-operator miner does not have. The remaining lines are already solved or already held: the three Docker bullets (:16-18) are satisfied by Dockerfile:2/58 (pinned `golang:1.25-alpine` -> `scratch`) and :109-110, whose HEALTHCHECK runs the binary's own `-healthcheck` probe because a scratch image has no shell -- while `node_modules` in .dockerignore is meaningless and "use a non-root user" contradicts a documented decision, README.md:1273-1281 explaining that the image runs as root so the self-updater can replace /twitch-miner-go, and giving the non-root recipe with its trade-off. Health/shutdown (:31-33) and Twelve-Factor config (:37) are exceeded by the internal/health package (1,661 non-test lines across 4 non-test files; 3,543 lines across all 8 including tests), `signal.NotifyContext` plus bounded teardown in cmd/miner/main.go, and internal/runtimeconfig's fail-closed startup gate; the production checklist's "pinned versions" (:52) restates github-actions-hardening references/supply-chain.md:6-29 (SHA-pinning; mutable tags are HIGH) in two words, and its "no hardcoded secrets" is that skill's SKILL.md secret-handling material, and CSP plus X-Frame-Options are already emitted at internal/web/security.go:117-120. What genuinely is NOT covered anywhere is a short list of un-elaborated nouns from the same checklist line -- container resource limits (absent from docker-compose.yml), JSON logs (which would fight internal/logger/console.go's human-readable handler by design), HSTS (correctly absent: the dashboard is plain HTTP on a LAN), TLS, CORS, rate limiting, a runbook and on-call -- several of which are deliberate positions rather than gaps, and none of which the skill elaborates with a value, a Go/GOMEMLIMIT rationale or a method. That is below the material-addition bar this manifest applies elsewhere (cf. documentation-writer). Rollback (:41) and Mobile Deployment (:55-61) additionally collide with CLAUDE.md's non-delegable "Release, tag, or deploy to any runtime environment" -- the ground that excluded github-release, applied here at the weaker dependabot weight since it is 2 of 10 sections rather than the whole skill -- and the artifact is a superset wrapper of the already-EXCLUDED multi-stage-dockerfile, carrying its same three Docker prescriptions and the same Node flavor (`NODE_ENV=production`, :37). Patching out two of ten sections to salvage that noun list is neither minimal patching nor repaid.

excluded_skills.name: incident-postmortem
excluded_skills.reason: Closest call in this slice. excluded_skills.name: sql-code-review
excluded_skills.reason: Wrong engines and wrong shape. Its 'Database-Specific Best Practices' section covers PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server and Oracle; grep -i sqlite over the file returns zero hits, and this project is SQLite-only. Its unit of review is standalone SQL scripts and DBA-facing concerns (GRANT/role permissions, index strategy, window functions, N+1 across an ORM), whereas here SQL lives inline in Go with a per-module `schema_versions` migration system — the actual correctness risks (migration ordering, single shared connection, cross-module version bumps) are not in scope for it. Nothing in this provider covers SQLite or schema migrations; that gap stays open.

excluded_skills.name: ui-screenshots
excluded_skills.reason: Near-duplicate of the installed anthropic webapp-testing for the part that applies here — both are Python Playwright against a local app, and webapp-testing already ships helper scripts (scripts/with_server.py, examples/console_logging.py) plus this repo's audit-before-exec patch. The remainder (~half the file) is Windows-only desktop capture via mss + ctypes/Win32 EnumWindows and Electron/VS Code capture over CDP, which is irrelevant to a Linux-built Go binary. The only novel ideas are the iterate-on-crop-not-on-capture discipline and the before/after-must-share-viewport-and-crop rule — worth a line in a manifest note, not a vendored skill.
